citation: Utility Supplier Cyber Security Addendum sec. 1 (flow-down of CIP-013-2 R1 Part 1.2.1); customer security terms register
trigger: Confirmation of a cyber incident related to TMUs, TMU firmware or configuration software, field service, or the FMS that poses cyber security risk to the utility
deadline: Within 24 hours of confirming the incident
notify: Security contact of each of the 45 utilities with a 24-hour term (from the register)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - exercise scenario: the firmware build servers that hold the signing key were encrypted, so the PSIRT treated the incident as related to supplied products for all 140 utilities
notifying_entity: Transformer Manufacturing PSIRT (Chief product security officer)
clock_starts: Confirmation that the incident relates to supplied products or services (the group SOC counts)

citation: Utility Supplier Cyber Security Addendum sec. 1 (flow-down of CIP-013-2 R1 Part 1.2.1)
trigger: Same as above
deadline: Within 48 hours of confirming the incident
notify: Security contact of each of the 95 utilities with a 48-hour term
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - same decision as the 24-hour group; group practice is to send all 140 notices within 24 hours
clock_starts: Confirmation that the incident relates to supplied products or services

obligation: Utility addendum response coordination and firmware integrity advice
citation: Utility Supplier Cyber Security Addendum secs. 2 and 5 (CIP-013-2 R1 Parts 1.2.2 and 1.2.5 flow-down)
trigger: Notice sent under sec. 1
deadline: Ongoing until closure: name the last known-good firmware releases and hashes; say whether utilities should hold firmware updates; report the key revocation
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

citation: Utility Supplier Cyber Security Addendum sec. 3 (CIP-013-2 R1 Part 1.2.3 flow-down)
trigger: A field technician's remote or on-site access to a utility should no longer be granted (for example, a compromised account)
deadline: Within 1 business day
applies_at_this_tier: Checked: no field service accounts were used in the exercise

obligation: Transformer Manufacturing notice to the Electric Utility (affiliate as vendor)
citation: POL-01 4.8 and POL-03 4.4; 2019 intercompany supply agreement (no notice term yet, POAM-017); the utility's CIP-013-2 plan expects vendor notice
trigger: Incident affecting TMU firmware, the 41 utility substations with TMUs, or affiliate deliveries
deadline: Group rule: within 24 hours, and at once on the group bridge
notify: Electric Utility NERC compliance director and CIP Senior Manager
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - same TMU firmware decision as the 140 utilities; also storm-season delivery impact
clock_starts: Confirmation that the incident relates to supplied products

citation: Purchase orders and supply agreements (delay and force majeure terms vary)
trigger: Production stop that delays committed deliveries or storm-reserve units
deadline: As each contract requires; group target within 2 business days of knowing a delivery date will slip
notify: Affected utility and industrial customers, including the Electric Utility storm desk
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all 8 plants stop when the MES buffer runs out (about 48 hours)
notifying_entity: VP manufacturing operations with the Group General Counsel
clock_starts: Knowledge that a committed date will be missed

citation: Client contracts (CIP-013-2 R1 Part 1.2.1 terms in 41 contracts; client terms register, POAM-012)
trigger: An incident related to the services Grid Engineering provides that poses cyber security risk to the client (for example, theft of client BCSI or CEII)
deadline: Per contract: 24, 48, or 72 hours after Grid Engineering identifies the incident
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - exercise scenario: closed-project archives of 17 clients with flow-down terms were taken from legacy group file servers
clock_starts: Identification of the incident (the group SOC counts)

obligation: Grid Engineering notice to other clients whose data was taken
trigger: Client confidential information in the stolen archives without CIP flow-down terms
deadline: As each contract requires; group target within 5 business days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 100 other clients appear in the archives

obligation: Grid Engineering notice to the Electric Utility (affiliate as vendor)
citation: POL-03 4.4; 2020 intercompany services agreement (no notice term yet, POAM-017)
trigger: Electric Utility BCSI or project files in the stolen data
deadline: Immediately on the group bridge (group rule)
notify: Electric Utility NERC compliance director and CIP Senior Manager
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 2021 TCC design documents from a closed affiliate project were in the archives
notifying_entity: Grid Engineering security and compliance lead

obligation: CIP-008-6 R4 Reportable Cyber Security Incident notification
trigger: Determination that a Cyber Security Incident compromised or disrupted a medium impact BES Cyber System, its ESP, or its EACMS at the TCC
deadline: Within 1 hour after the determination; include functional impact, attack vector, and level of intrusion to the extent known
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - medium impact BES Cyber Systems at the TCC. In the exercise the EAP was probed but not compromised, so this row was not triggered
notifying_entity: Electric Utility (NERC compliance director; CIP Senior Manager approves determinations)
clock_starts: Determination of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident

obligation: CIP-008-6 R4 attempt to compromise notification
trigger: Determination, using the plan's criteria, that a Cyber Security Incident was an attempt to compromise a medium impact BES Cyber System, its ESP, or its EACMS
deadline: By the end of the next calendar day after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - exercise scenario: scans and login attempts against the TCC Electronic Access Point from a compromised corporate server
notifying_entity: Electric Utility (NERC compliance director; CIP Senior Manager approves determinations)
clock_starts: Determination of an attempt to compromise

trigger: New or changed information about a reported incident or attempt
deadline: Within 7 calendar days of determining new or changed information
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
notifying_entity: Electric Utility (NERC compliance director; CIP Senior Manager approves determinations)

obligation: E-ISAC notice of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident at a low impact asset
trigger: A Cyber Security Incident that compromised or disrupted a low impact BES Cyber System at one of the 58 transmission substations
deadline: CIP-003-9 sets no fixed time; notification follows the determination. Group target: within 1 hour of the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Checked: no substation activity in the exercise
notifying_entity: Electric Utility (NERC compliance director; CIP Senior Manager approves determinations)
clock_starts: Determination of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident

citation: Form DOE-417 criteria 2 and 3; Federal Energy Administration Act of 1974 sec. 13(b) (Pub. L. 93-275); OMB 1901-0288
trigger: Criterion 2: a Reportable Cyber Security Incident. Criterion 3: a cyber event that is not a Reportable Cyber Security Incident but causes interruption of electrical system operations
deadline: Within 1 hour of the incident (telephone notice to the DOE Emergency Operations Center is acceptable when operations are critical, followed by the form)
notify: DOE (DOE-417 online system); the form can be shared with NERC, the E-ISAC, and CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Checked: not met in the exercise (no interruption of electrical system operations)
notifying_entity: Electric Utility (TCC or DCC shift supervisor starts; NERC compliance director files)

trigger: Criterion 11: a cyber event that could potentially affect electric power system adequacy or reliability. Criterion 12: loss of electric service to more than 50,000 customers for 1 hour or more
deadline: Within 6 hours of the incident if no Emergency Alert criterion applies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - decision rule agreed with counsel (P03 EU-G47): the utility files a precautionary Normal Report under criterion 11 when it isolates group IT from the TCC or DCC, as it did in the exercise
clock_starts: The incident (the isolation decision is recorded with the time)

trigger: A Cyber Security Incident that was an attempt to compromise high or medium impact BES Cyber Systems or their EACMS
deadline: By the end of the next calendar day after the determination, if no earlier criterion applies; check box 14 on the earlier form when both apply
notify: DOE; the form can carry the CIP-008-6 notice to the E-ISAC and CISA if the utility asks DOE to share it
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the TCC EAP probing; reported on the same form as the criterion 11 Normal Report

trigger: Significant new information; every filed report
deadline: Update when significant information becomes available; final report (updated Schedule 1 and all of Schedule 2) within 72 hours of the incident
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

citation: NERC EOP-004-4 R2 and Attachment 1 (TO, TOP, DP events)
trigger: For example: complete loss of monitoring or control capability at a BES control center for 30 continuous minutes or more; damage or destruction of its Facility from actual or suspected intentional human action
deadline: By the later of 24 hours after recognizing that a threshold was met or the end of the next business day (4 p.m. local time)
notify: NERC (systemawareness@nerc.net) and the parties in the Operating Plan; a DOE-417 form may be used as the report
applies_at_this_tier: Checked: not met in the exercise (TCC monitoring and control unaffected; no Facility damage)
clock_starts: Recognition that a threshold was met

obligation: Voluntary report to CISA and the FBI
trigger: Ransomware in any division, or any intrusion into OT
deadline: As soon as practicable (group target: same day)
notify: CISA (report.cisa.gov or CISA Central); FBI field office
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary; supports response help and OFAC mitigation

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
citation: 6 U.S.C. 681b; proposed 6 CFR 226.5 (proposed; critical manufacturing criterion)
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-10-05 (proposed only); readiness only

obligation: DoD cyber incident reporting for covered defense information
trigger: Cyber incident affecting covered defense information or operationally critical support
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - no DoD contracts and no covered defense information in any division (P03 G-101)

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Identification of covered telecommunications equipment or services during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: Only if found while rebuilding or inventorying systems used on the 14 Manufacturing or the Grid Engineering federal contracts; not triggered in the exercise
notifying_entity: Director of federal contracts; Grid Engineering federal programs manager

trigger: Identification of a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) during contract performance
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: Only if found during the response; not triggered
notifying_entity: Director of federal contracts; Grid Engineering federal programs manager

trigger: Identification of a covered article subject to an applicable FASCSA order
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: Only for the 9 Manufacturing contracts that include the clause, and only if found; not triggered

citation: Each federal contract's delivery and delay terms (FAR 52.204-21 has no incident reporting duty)
trigger: Production stop that delays a federal delivery
deadline: As each contract requires
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 3 federal deliveries were scheduled in the 30 days after the exercise start

trigger: Determination that a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the holding company is an SEC registrant; a stop at all 8 plants (about $26.3 million of output a day) is a likely material incident

trigger: Annual report
deadline: With the Form 10-K
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - describe risk management, strategy, and governance; consider lessons from the incident

citation: State breach notification statutes; worked example Fla. Stat. 501.171(4)
trigger: Breach of personal information (for example, name with Social Security number) of residents
deadline: Varies by state; Florida: no later than 30 days after determination (a 15-day extension for good cause applies only to this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - exercise scenario: legacy HR exports with Social Security numbers of about 31,000 current and former employees and applicants (about 14,000 in Florida) were taken
notifying_entity: Each employing subsidiary, through the Group Chief Privacy Officer

trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more Florida residents (other states set their own thresholds and recipients)
deadline: Florida: no later than 30 days after determination (no extension)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs; other states' regulators as their laws require
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 14,000 Florida residents in the exercise

trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - more than 1,000 individuals

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the covered entity
trigger: Corporate shared services, which maintains HR data for each employing subsidiary, discovers a breach of that data
deadline: Within 10 days after determination; the group rule is the same day, on the bridge
notify: Each employing subsidiary's president and the Group Chief Privacy Officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - corporate maintains the HR exports for the three divisions' employing entities

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any payment to an extortionist
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; the exercise included a demand

trigger: An incident affecting FMS data or availability
deadline: As each subscription agreement requires
applies_at_this_tier: Checked: the FMS (provider B) was not affected in the exercise

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier hotline before hiring response vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal
